chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arfah narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Abu Hafs al-Abbar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Juhadah, from Bakir ibn 'Abdullah al-Madani, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:

Beware of stinginess (al-shuḥ), for it was by stinginess that those before you were destroyed. It commanded you to lie, so you lied; it commanded you to oppress, so you oppressed; and it commanded you to cut off ties, so you cut off ties.

key_terms.الشُّحّ: Stinginess coupled with greed or covetousness of the soul

ai.seo_question: What are the three consequences of stinginess (shuḥ) according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights 'al-shuḥ' not merely as financial stinginess but as a deep-seated soul covetousness that precipitates moral collapse. This hadith establishes a causal chain where greed compels individuals to lie, practice oppression, and sever kinship ties, mirroring the fate of earlier nations. It serves as a foundational ethical warning in Shia tradition, linking internal spiritual decay to external social disintegration.
